cells.title: Offer a project's own static checks at onboarding
cells.action: Implement docs/history/trust-layers/CONTEXT.md D1 as refined by D5, and contract C1. Anchors in onboard/notices.rs: `pub fn detect_commands(root: &Path) -> Vec<Candidate> {`, `pub fn commands_notices(repo_root: &Path, first_onboard: bool) -> Vec<String> {`, the predicate `let recorded = COMMAND_KEYS.iter().any(|key| {` inside it, and `fn declares_test(commands: Option<&serde_json::Map<String, Value>>) -> bool {`; in onboard/templates.rs: `pub const NO_TEST_VERIFICATION_OFFER` (the offer posture to follow). (1) Detector. Add a static-check detector beside detect_commands, with its own result type (do not reuse Candidate, whose key comes from COMMAND_KEYS): input the repo root; output at most one candidate per kind, the kinds being lint and type check; each candidate carries the command, the source file and a marker word. It reads the project's own root files only and runs no tool. Lint kind, first hit wins: a package.json script named lint; a Makefile target named lint; a composer.json script named lint; Cargo.toml (`cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, marker clippy); pyproject.toml holding a `[tool.ruff` table (`ruff check .`, marker ruff); go.mod (`go vet ./...`, marker vet). Type-check kind, first hit wins: a package.json script named typecheck or type-check; a Makefile target named typecheck; pyproject.toml holding a `[tool.mypy` table (`mypy .`, marker mypy). For a manifest script the marker word is the script name. For a package.json script the runner follows the lockfile at the root: pnpm-lock.yaml gives `pnpm run <name>`, yarn.lock gives `yarn <name>`, bun.lockb or bun.lock gives `bun run <name>`, otherwise `npm run <name>`. A malformed manifest yields no candidate from that file and never panics. (2) Recorded rule (D5). In commands_notices a test command counts as recorded when commands.test is a non-empty string or a non-empty list (the declares_test rule); setup and start keep their string rule. So a list-valued commands.test no longer draws the `No standard commands recorded` notice; this is an intended fix, and a test must pin it. (3) Notices. Case (a): no command recorded and at least one static check detected: the existing first notice (either arm) gains one sentence that lists the static checks with their sources and says to offer them as the first members of the `commands.test` list, before the tests. Case (b): a test command is recorded and it is not the sentinel none, and at least one detected check has its marker word in no commands.test entry: return one notice that lists those checks with their sources and says to offer adding them before the tests in the `commands.test` list. Both cases also say: run each proposed check once first and tell the user whether it is green or how many findings it reports; look through the project's recorded decisions for an earlier answer about that check and stay silent about a check the user already refused; record the user's answer for each check as a decision; never write an unconfirmed value. Case (c): commands.test is the sentinel none, or nothing is detected, or only setup or start is recorded: return exactly what the function returns today for that config (for a list-valued test with nothing detected that is now an empty list, per (2)). The Greenfield notice text does not change. Keep fixed notice text as constants in templates.rs. Red first, with test names that contain static_check: one candidate per kind and manifest beats convention; the lockfile picks the runner; a malformed package.json; case (a) for both arms; case (b) fires for a string and for a list that lacks the marker word and is silent when an entry contains it (for example `pnpm lint` or `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`); a list-valued commands.test with nothing detected returns nothing; the none sentinel; and with no candidate the two existing arms equal today's exact strings. No code comments. The proof run must show the new tests ran: quote the count of tests the filter matched, which must be above zero.

A project whose commands.test already has an entry containing the check's marker word gets no static-check notice
A project with no command recorded and a static check found gets the existing notice plus the static checks, offered first in the commands.test list
A list-valued commands.test counts as recorded and no longer draws the No standard commands recorded notice
With no candidate detected, or commands.test set to none, a string-valued or empty config gets exactly the strings it got before
Each static-check notice tells the agent to run the check once before offering it and to record the user's answer as a decision
The detector reads files only and runs no tool

cells.title: Write the static-rules craft page and wire the doctrine
cells.action: Implement docs/history/trust-layers/CONTEXT.md D2 and the doctrine half of D3. Load the bee-technical-writing skill first; the craft page is a how-to guide, one type per file. (1) Write expertise/static-rules.md in the voice and frontmatter shape of the other craft pages in expertise/ (read expertise/tests.md for the shape). Content, generic to any project, never about bee itself: when a mistake's fix-at layer is check, pick the highest of four homes that can hold the rule, in this order: a type the compiler enforces (make the wrong value impossible to build), a rule in the linter the project already runs, a test, a hook or guard. For the lint home, name where a project rule usually lives per ecosystem: ESLint (no-restricted-syntax, no-restricted-imports, or a local rule), Clippy (disallowed-methods and disallowed-types in clippy.toml), Ruff (banned-api under flake8-tidy-imports), golangci-lint (forbidigo, depguard), and a pattern rule tool such as ast-grep or Semgrep when the project's linter cannot express the rule. State the proof: show the new rule red on the past mistake, then green after the fix; a rule never seen red proves only that it loads. State where the rule must run: it has to be a member of the project's commands.test list, or CI never sees it. State that a tool the project does not already run is the owner's decision: ask before adding one. State how to stage the red proof: rebuild the past mistake as a small fixture or a scratch edit, show the rule red on it, then remove it so it does not stay in the tree. State the dead end: when the project has no commands.test list, or it is the sentinel none, take the question to the owner instead of writing a rule nothing runs. Add a one-line list of rule homes for other ecosystems (.NET banned-API analyzers, ErrorProne or ArchUnit for Java, detekt for Kotlin, RuboCop custom cops, PHPStan custom rules, SwiftLint custom_rules, Credo), and say that a project with no compiler-checked types starts at the lint home. State when not to write a rule: a one-off, or a rule with false positives that people will switch off. Keep it under 140 lines. (2) Add one row for static-rules.md to the Craft table of expertise/INDEX.md. (3) In skills/bee-capturing/references/promotion.md, step 2 of the Promotion Decision Tree (anchor: `2. Mechanizable? A grep/lint line in a verify command, a guard, a hook`), add one sentence that points to `.bee/expertise/static-rules.md` for which home to pick and how to prove it. (4) In packages/bee/LEADER.md, in the bullet that starts `Write a mistake down the MOMENT you notice it` (anchor: `bee mailbox reflect --wrong "<what went wrong>"`), add at most three lines: a correction from the user of how you worked (not a new instruction or a changed requirement) is a mistake too, recorded the same way with `--source user` the moment it is given, with the user's own words kept in `--wrong` so a repeat matches; an accepted P1 or P2 review finding takes `--source review`; the same key seen twice is a fix-first candidate whatever its source. (5) Run the regen chain: `.bee/bin/bee dev regen`, then `.bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --write`, then `.bee/bin/bee onboard --repo-root . --json` and, when it reports changes_needed, `.bee/bin/bee onboard --repo-root . --apply --json`, so .bee/LEADER.md, .bee/expertise/ and the vendored skill trees match their sources. `.bee/bin/bee` in this worktree is the installed binary of the main checkout; the regen chain reads the source files of this worktree, so that binary is the right one to run. In a worktree the onboard report may still list runtime files such as .bee/reservations.json as changes_needed; that is expected, and no skill, expertise or leader file may remain in its plan after the apply. Never hand-edit a vendored tree. If a parity test pins a line count or a rule list of LEADER.md, keep the new lines inside the existing rule block and update the pinned value only where the test names it. Cite CONTEXT.md D-numbers in prose, never raw decision ids. One commit.

Anchors: `fn build_digest` (it builds the digest object), `fn digest_summary_line` (the one printed sentence, where the mistakes witness already adds a clause), `fn collect_feedback(root: &Path) -> Option<CollectData> {` (it already walks .bee/backlog.jsonl row by row and reads each row's layer), and the test `the_digest_counts_clean_run_answers_against_real_reflections` (how a digest test builds its fixture). The functions collect_counts, counts_value and summary_line serve bee feedback count: do not change them, and the counts object stays byte-identical. Add one top-level key prose_load to the digest object. It holds: for each of AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and LEADER.md that exists at the repo root, its path and line count, and their sum as the project lines; the line count of .bee/LEADER.md as the bee lines; the number of critical patterns, counted as the top-level list lines (lines that start with `- `) under the `## Critical patterns` heading of docs/knowledge/index.md up to the next `## ` heading; and the number of rows filed in .bee/backlog.jsonl whose layer is exactly fix-at:check and the number whose layer is exactly fix-at:architecture, tallied from the raw rows in the existing backlog walk, before any row is dropped or folded. A file that is a symbolic link to another counted file is counted once. A source that is absent (no such file, no such section, no backlog) reads as null in the object, never as zero, following the existing witness, which uses null for not measured. An unreadable or malformed row is skipped. Nothing here fails or refuses the digest. Add one clause to the printed digest sentence that names, in plain words, the project lines, the bee lines, the critical pattern count and the two counts of rows filed; an absent source prints as not present, never as 0. It is a witness: it refuses nothing, drops nothing, and adds no score or threshold. The digest carries counts and the fixed file names only, never file content. Red first, with test names that contain prose_load: a fixture root with AGENTS.md, a .bee/LEADER.md, an index with three top-level critical pattern lines and one nested line, and a backlog with two check rows and one architecture row yields those exact numbers in the object and in the printed sentence; a CLAUDE.md that is a symbolic link to AGENTS.md is not counted twice (unix only: gate that test with cfg(unix)); an empty root yields nulls, the words not present, and a successful digest; the counts object of an empty root is unchanged. No code comments. The proof run must show the new tests ran: quote the count of tests the filter matched, which must be above zero.

truths: The digest object holds a top-level prose_load with project lines, bee lines, the critical pattern count and the two fix-at row counts
The printed digest sentence names project lines, bee lines, critical patterns and rows filed
An absent source reads as null in the object and as not present in the sentence, and the digest still succeeds
bee feedback count and the counts object are unchanged
The digest holds no content of the instruction files

cells.title: Write the static-rules craft page and wire the doctrine
cells.action: Implement docs/history/trust-layers/CONTEXT.md D2 and the doctrine half of D3. Load the bee-technical-writing skill first; the craft page is a how-to guide, one type per file. (1) Write expertise/static-rules.md in the voice and frontmatter shape of the other craft pages in expertise/ (read expertise/tests.md for the shape). Content, generic to any project, never about bee itself: when a mistake's fix-at layer is check, pick the highest of four homes that can hold the rule, in this order: a type the compiler enforces (make the wrong value impossible to build), a rule in the linter the project already runs, a test, a hook or guard. For the lint home, name where a project rule usually lives per ecosystem: ESLint (no-restricted-syntax, no-restricted-imports, or a local rule), Clippy (disallowed-methods and disallowed-types in clippy.toml), Ruff (banned-api under flake8-tidy-imports), golangci-lint (forbidigo, depguard), and a pattern rule tool such as ast-grep or Semgrep when the project's linter cannot express the rule. State the proof: show the new rule red on the past mistake, then green after the fix; a rule never seen red proves only that it loads. State where the rule must run: it has to be a member of the project's commands.test list, or CI never sees it. State that a tool the project does not already run is the owner's decision: ask before adding one. State how to stage the red proof: rebuild the past mistake as a small fixture or a scratch edit, show the rule red on it, then remove it so it does not stay in the tree. State the dead end: when the project has no commands.test list, or it is the sentinel none, take the question to the owner instead of writing a rule nothing runs. Add a one-line list of rule homes for other ecosystems (.NET banned-API analyzers, ErrorProne or ArchUnit for Java, detekt for Kotlin, RuboCop custom cops, PHPStan custom rules, SwiftLint custom_rules, Credo), and say that a project with no compiler-checked types starts at the lint home. State when not to write a rule: a one-off, or a rule with false positives that people will switch off. Keep it under 140 lines. (2) Add one row for static-rules.md to the Craft table of expertise/INDEX.md. (3) In skills/bee-capturing/references/promotion.md, step 2 of the Promotion Decision Tree (anchor: `2. Mechanizable? A grep/lint line in a verify command, a guard, a hook`), add one sentence that points to `.bee/expertise/static-rules.md` for which home to pick and how to prove it. (4) In packages/bee/LEADER.md, in the bullet that starts `Write a mistake down the MOMENT you notice it` (anchor: `bee mailbox reflect --wrong "<what went wrong>"`), add at most three lines: a correction from the user of how you worked (not a new instruction or a changed requirement) is a mistake too, recorded the same way with `--source user` the moment it is given, with the user's own words kept in `--wrong` so a repeat matches; an accepted P1 or P2 review finding takes `--source review`; the same key seen twice is a fix-first candidate whatever its source. (5) Run the regen chain: `.bee/bin/bee dev regen`, then `.bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --write`, then `.bee/bin/bee onboard --repo-root . --json` and, when it reports changes_needed, `.bee/bin/bee onboard --repo-root . --apply --json`, so .bee/LEADER.md, .bee/expertise/ and the vendored skill trees match their sources. `.bee/bin/bee` in this worktree is the installed binary of the main checkout; the regen chain reads the source files of this worktree, so that binary is the right one to run. In a worktree the onboard report may still list runtime files such as .bee/reservations.json as changes_needed; that is expected, and no skill, expertise or leader file may remain in its plan after the apply. Never hand-edit a vendored tree. If a parity test pins a line count or a rule list of LEADER.md, keep the new lines inside the existing rule block and update the pinned value only where the test names it. Cite CONTEXT.md D-numbers in prose, never raw decision ids. One commit.
cells.verify: .bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check && .bee/bin/bee onboard --repo-root . --json && cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --test rule_index_parity --test pointer_integrity --test instruction_laws
